question: What was the charge-coupled device, the sensor in early digital cameras, first invented to do?
answer: To store data. In 1969 Willard Boyle and George Smith at Bell Labs designed it as a memory, passing packets of charge along a chip like buckets in a line. Light also frees charge in silicon, so the same bucket brigade could read out an image. The memory never caught on; the camera sensor earned them the 2009 Nobel Prize.
move: An invention often succeeds at a job it was never designed for.
